title: Seasonal energy exchange in sea ice retreat regions contributes to differences in projected Arctic warming
problem: Climate models significantly disagree on the magnitude of projected Arctic warming (inter-model spread), and the specific mechanisms driving this disagreement, particularly seasonal energy exchanges in sea ice retreat regions, are not well understood, which hinders efforts to reduce uncertainty in climate projections.
method: The paper proposes a regional, process-oriented surface energy budget decomposition to partition temperature changes into contributions from individual climate processes, thereby identifying seasonal energy exchanges in sea ice retreat regions as the source of inter-model spread in projected Arctic warming.
task: The task is to explain the inter-model spread in projected Arctic warming by analyzing how differences in seasonal energy exchanges within sea ice retreat regions, specifically summer solar absorption and fall/winter heat release, contribute to disagreements among climate models on the magnitude of future warming.
innovation: This paper attributes the inter-model spread in projected Arctic warming to model differences in simulating seasonal energy transfer in sea ice retreat regions, where summer solar heat is stored in the ocean and released as turbulent fluxes in fall/winter.
